system_description.narrative_title: Global bond-market selloff: rising yields, inflation, and failed interventions
system_description.narrative_summary: A global bond-market selloff driven by hotter-than-expected inflation and a sharp oil-price shock is pushing government yields to multi-year highs and rebuilding expectations of further central-bank tightening. Market interventions (notably Scott Bessent’s Treasury buyback) have so far failed to calm the long end, amplifying spillovers to credit costs, fiscal interest bills and equity/FX markets. Feedback loops between commodity shocks, sticky inflation and policy tightening are making the system highly sensitive to small new data or events.
system_description.scope: Global government bond markets and yields, central-bank policy expectations and rate decisions, inflation and oil-price dynamics, large market interventions (Treasury buybacks, sanctions signalling), investor positioning and short-term market liquidity; and direct spillovers to credit, fiscal interest costs, equities and FX.
system_description.super_system: Global macro-financial system / world economy and monetary-financial order
adjacent_subsystems: Private credit and banking sector (corporate borrowing costs, covenant stress)

variables.name: Long-term government bond yield
variables.description: The prevailing interest rate investors require for long-maturity sovereign debt, reflecting compensation for time, inflation and risk over extended horizons.

variables.name: Short-term policy interest rate
variables.description: The benchmark overnight or short-maturity policy interest rate set by monetary authorities that anchors short-term funding costs.

variables.name: Headline inflation rate
variables.description: The observed year-on-year change in a broad price index capturing overall consumer price inflation including volatile components.

variables.name: Inflation persistence
variables.description: The rate at which elevated inflationary pressures decay or are sustained over time, indicating stickiness in price dynamics.

variables.name: Long-term inflation expectations
variables.description: Market and agent expectations for average inflation over multi-year horizons as revealed by surveys, breakevens or forward indicators.

variables.name: Commodity price level
variables.description: The aggregate price level of key commodities (notably energy) that feeds directly into production costs and consumer prices.

variables.name: Commodity price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of swings in commodity prices, capturing uncertainty and shock intensity in commodity markets.

variables.name: Central-bank tightening expectations
variables.description: The market-implied likelihood and anticipated magnitude of future monetary policy rate increases by central authorities.

variables.name: Bond term premium
variables.description: The extra yield investors demand to hold longer-duration bonds versus a sequence of expected short rates, reflecting risk and liquidity compensation.

variables.name: Short-term market liquidity
variables.description: The ease and cost of executing large transactions in fixed-income markets without significantly moving prices over short horizons.

variables.name: Investor risk positioning
variables.description: The aggregate net exposure of market participants to risk assets, indicating propensity to buy or sell in response to shocks.

variables.name: Aggregate investor leverage
variables.description: The average level of borrowed exposure across investors in financial markets, amplifying gains and losses when positions are adjusted.

variables.name: Market intervention activity
variables.description: The flow and intensity of purposeful market operations (e.g., large-scale asset purchases or sales) executed to influence prices or liquidity.

variables.name: Credit spread level
variables.description: The average premium investors demand for holding non-sovereign debt over risk-free sovereign bonds, reflecting credit and liquidity risk.

variables.name: Public sector interest burden
variables.description: The ongoing flow of government interest payments relative to the size of the economy, indicating fiscal sensitivity to yields.

variables.name: Equity market valuation level
variables.description: The average pricing of equities relative to fundamentals (e.g., earnings), capturing sensitivity of equity prices to changes in rates and risk sentiment.

catalysts.title: FOMC rate decision (mid‑September)
catalysts.description: Scheduled Fed policy decision expected to raise the policy rate; market consensus and headlines signal a high chance of another hike. The decision will directly alter short‑term policy rates and reshape rate‑expectation pricing.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'The Fed Is Poised for a Rate Hike', 'All Eyes on Fed Rate Decision', 'Firm Inflation Reading Pushes Fed Closer to a Rate Increase'.

catalysts.title: BOJ set to lift rates
catalysts.description: Bank of Japan expected to raise its policy rate next week, a notable policy shift that will alter short‑term rates and affect global carry and yield curves.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'BOJ set to lift rates next week but offer few clues on terminal'.

catalysts.title: Sustained oil-price surge
catalysts.description: Oil has jumped sharply and further price increases or persistent elevation would feed directly into headline inflation and rate‑hopes across central banks, sustaining yield pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Global bond selloff reignites as oil jumps to $109', 'surging oil prices inflame inflation risks'.

catalysts.title: Follow‑on Treasury/buyback interventions
catalysts.description: Additional buybacks or large-scale purchases (private or Treasury‑led) are likely as market actors try to cap yields; effectiveness is uncertain and will influence liquidity and yields.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Treasury Plans $6 Billion Buyback', 'Bessent’s beefed-up buyback operation fails to calm market'.

catalysts.title: ECB further‑rate hikes (possible)
catalysts.description: ECB officials have signalled additional hikes are conditional on energy-driven inflation; further tightening would raise short‑term rates and European yields over coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'ECB policymakers open door to more rate hikes', 'ECB prepares for ‘longer‑lasting’ inflation as it lifts interest rates to 2.5%'.

catalysts.title: Rapid market repricing of tightening expectations
catalysts.description: Markets are repricing a more aggressive multi‑hike Fed path after hotter inflation prints, pushing yields and term premium higher in the short term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Firm Inflation Reading Pushes Fed Closer to a Rate Increase', 'The Fed could raise interest rates three times.'

catalysts.title: Deleveraging / margin‑call pressure
catalysts.description: Widening yields and credit stress are likely to trigger margin calls and deleveraging in private credit and leveraged positions, reducing liquidity and risk appetite.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Lenders say show me the money as bond carnage spreads', 'The oil shock is testing private credit borrowers already burdened by high debt costs'.

catalysts.title: Planned U.S. sanction on 'large' bank (Monday)
catalysts.description: Announced sanction on an unnamed large bank is scheduled for the coming Monday; such action could disrupt interbank flows and market confidence, pressuring liquidity and risk sentiment.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump administration to sanction unnamed 'large' bank on Monday, Bessent says'.

catalysts.title: Rising public‑sector interest burden
catalysts.description: Higher yields are increasing governments' interest bills, pressuring fiscal balances and potentially prompting issuance or fiscal adjustments through year‑end.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'France’s debt interest bill to jump 25% this year', 'The world’s $2tn interest bill'.
